A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OT Score research. Their complete main texts and appendices A–E, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original confidence-score evaluations, adaptation accuracies, model-comparison results and synthetic experiments in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds DomainNet-126 evaluation and optimization-sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Both versions use source class means, the same semi-discrete OT score and the same 2·OT·JMDS reweighting with pre-adaptation features. v3 explicitly writes the minibatch average in Algorithm 1, clarifying the batch-based computation already described in v2 rather than establishing a different underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds seven DomainNet-126 transfer tasks among the S/P/C/R domains for the reweighting evaluation (Table 4). This extends image-domain coverage within the existing classification task family; the earlier benchmarks, digit comparisons and synthetic scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DATUM and PS on Office-Home, and Table 3 adds TPDS on VisDA. The new DomainNet comparison also evaluates previously absent comparators including AaD, PLUE, SF(DA)2 and UCon-SFDA. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set while retaining baselines in the corresponding earlier experiments.

E3.justification: The new Section 5.4 experiment sweeps seven regularization values from 10^-8 to 0.5 on Office-Home Art→Clipart, using a common warm-start initialization and optimization diagnostics. Existing evaluation protocols, training settings and the default regularization value of 10^-4 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix D.3 add a focused regularization-sensitivity study measuring marginal residual, dual updates, objective convergence, assignment entropy and the Top1–Top2 probability gap. It tests optimization stability on one transfer task; the earlier robustness, synthetic and model-comparison analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent seeds and mean ± standard deviation for Office-Home and VisDA in Appendix D.2. Those uncertainty summaries are retained unchanged. The added DomainNet table and diagnostic curves introduce no new uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands reported results with DomainNet scores, additional baseline rows and optimization diagnostics. Table 4 reports 70.9% average accuracy for OTScore, 66.9% for CoWA and 70.8% for UCon-SFDA. Existing results remain unchanged, including OTScore's 73.0% Office-Home and 87.8% VisDA averages; these are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds a corrected soft-assignment definition using w_ell in the denominator, whereas v2's displayed formula repeats w_j. This is a limited mathematical correction, although v3's Algorithm 1 still retains the old index. The theoretical bounds and Appendix C/E proofs remain unchanged; Theorem 8 mainly clarifies notation.

C1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction qualify the adaptation setting as prototype-assisted or explicitly using source class-mean features. This narrows the stated applicability to match inputs already used in v2. The central theoretical, confidence-estimation, reweighting and model-selection contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly clarifies that target clustering assumptions motivate the sufficient conditions rather than being required to compute OT scores. Section 5.4 and Appendix D.3 add interpretations of stable optimization and nearly hard assignments at small regularization values. Existing class-proportion limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a linked code-availability statement and makes the soft-assignment formula and minibatch reduction more explicit. Appendix D.2 retains the earlier hardware, backbone, optimizer and training-budget information. The new DomainNet evaluation receives little additional implementation detail beyond its ResNet-50 specification.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds works associated with DATUM, PS, AaD, TPDS, SF(DA)2 and UCon-SFDA. These update the comparison context, while Appendix A's related-work discussion and the main positioning relative to OT theory and confidence estimation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and author block, clarifies terminology and notation, and introduces Section 5.4 and Appendix D.3. Most existing prose and the overall section-and-appendix organization are retained, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reformats the document with different typography, a wider text block, revised headings and author layout, and reflowed equations and floats. It expands comparison tables and adds the DomainNet table and two diagnostic figures. Earlier figures are retained, resized or relocated rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Explicit prototype-assisted framing better matches the method's existing requirements. DomainNet comparisons and controlled regularization diagnostics strengthen empirical support, while the code link improves access information. These are useful incremental gains; limited DomainNet-specific protocol and uncertainty reporting, together with the remaining formula inconsistency, constrain the overall improvement.
